newsitem.title: UK: UK's IMRO fines Sovereign Unit Trust 225,000 stg.
newsitem.headline: UK's IMRO fines Sovereign Unit Trust 225,000 stg.

text.p: British investments watchdog the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) said on Thursday it had fined Sovereign Unit Trust Managers Ltd 225,000 pounds ($377,000) for rule breaches.

IMRO said Sovereign had agreed to a settlement of disciplinary proceedings for failures in its internal organisation, incorrectly pricing eight unit trusts and allowing three of its trusts to incorrectly pay fees which it should have paid itself.

IMRO said the breaches had taken place between April 1988 and September 1995. Sovereign has paid compensation of 120,000 pounds ($201,000) to 3,373 unit holders and 1.27 million pounds into the unit trusts. It will also pay IMRO's costs of 77,506 pounds.
It said Sovereign had "failed to control its internal affairs in a responsible manner" and had failed to take reasonable steps to prevent eight unit trusts being incorrectly priced.
The pricing errors were the due to inadequate staff training, internal control procedures, organisation and supervision, IMRO added.
Sovereign is based in Bournemouth in the south of England and has been regulated by IMRO since 1987. ($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
